title: Genetics
tagline: Mendel’s laws, chromosomes and meiosis, sex linkage, genetic maps, mutation, and the genetics of microbes and organelles
summary: Genetics explains how traits pass from parents to offspring and why relatives resemble each other. This course follows the classical route: Mendel’s laws and their extensions, the chromosome theory of inheritance, sex linkage and pedigrees, recombination and genetic maps, chromosome and gene mutations, the genetics of bacteria and viruses, and inheritance that breaks Mendel’s rules.

chapters.title: Mendelian inheritance
chapters.summary: Segregation and independent assortment, Punnett squares, test crosses and probability in genetics.

chapters.title: Extensions of Mendelian genetics
chapters.summary: Incomplete dominance and codominance, multiple and lethal alleles, epistasis, and the interplay of genes and environment.

chapters.title: Chromosomes and meiosis
chapters.summary: The chromosome theory of inheritance, meiosis as the physical basis of Mendel’s laws, and sex determination.

chapters.title: Sex linkage and pedigrees
chapters.summary: X-linked inheritance, dosage compensation and the analysis of human pedigrees.

chapters.title: Linkage and genetic maps
chapters.summary: Recombination frequency, map distances, three-point crosses and interference.

chapters.title: Chromosome mutations
chapters.summary: Changes in chromosome number and structure: aneuploidy, polyploidy, deletions, duplications, inversions and translocations.

chapters.title: Genes, DNA and mutation
chapters.summary: DNA as the genetic material, the gene concept, point mutations, mutagens and complementation tests.

chapters.title: Genetics of bacteria and viruses
chapters.summary: Transformation, conjugation and transduction, and how genes were mapped in microbes.

chapters.title: Non-Mendelian inheritance
chapters.summary: Maternal effects, mitochondrial and chloroplast inheritance, genomic imprinting and other exceptions to Mendel’s rules.
